correctness.rationale: An exact symmetric congruence transforms Euclidean norm loss into a Loewner inequality involving the original generator and the symmetrized surrogate perturbation. A second symmetric congruence gives the inverse-generator weighted energy. For positive rank-one surrogate changes, the associated symmetric matrix has one negative eigenmode exactly when the surrogate direction is not an eigenvector of the original SPD generator; the eigenvalue is half the negative Cauchy–Schwarz defect. The sharp inclusive step ceiling and exact boundary follow without finite testing. Similarity to a symmetric contractive map establishes spectral stability. An explicit rational two-dimensional example realizes the boundary and strict norm growth. A standalone checker passes 1,792 exact rational configurations and both witnesses, but the infinite statements rely on the analytical proof.

value.rationale: An implicit stage that is stronger dissipatively in Loewner order may still produce Euclidean transient growth when the exact generator is used for the output slope. The sharp all-dimensional one-step damping budget depends on a precise A-dependent alignment invariant and identifies the sole geometric all-step exception. This gives a usable exact surrogate-direction design criterion and separates Euclidean energy, inverse-generator weighted energy, and asymptotic spectral stability. Those are meaningful numerical stability issues in mixed-stage implicit methods, beyond a trivial single evaluation or renamed identity.
